claims.explanation: Amisulpride is a dopamine D2/D3 receptor antagonist, and its selective antiproliferative effect across cancer lines likely reflects dependence on dopamine receptor signaling or related GPCR/neuroendocrine programs in a subset of tumors. The most consistent genomic pattern among sensitive lines is co-occurrence of TP53 mutation with PI3K/AKT pathway activation (PIK3CA mutation/amplification, PTEN loss) and/or ARID1A loss, suggesting that cells with defective p53 and activated PI3K signaling are more vulnerable to D2 antagonism, perhaps through dopamine-modulated PI3K/AKT or cAMP signaling. Lineages enriched among sensitive lines (gastric, esophageal, endometrial, Ewing sarcoma, melanoma) may express DRD2 or related dopamine receptors, making them responsive to amisulpride.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is nearly universal in sensitive lines and may impair apoptotic response to dopamine receptor blockade
PIK3CA mutation/amplification is enriched in sensitive lines and may cooperate with D2 antagonism via PI3K/AKT signaling
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and appears in several sensitive lines, potentially increasing dependence on dopamine-modulated survival signals
ARID1A mutation is frequent in sensitive lines and may alter chromatin accessibility at dopamine receptor or neuroendocrine gene loci
Amisulpride's primary target is DRD2; lines expressing DRD2 are expected to be more responsive
Amisulpride also binds D3 receptors with high affinity, so DRD3 expression may mediate sensitivity
BRAF mutation appears in several sensitive melanoma and thyroid lines, possibly linking MAPK activation to dopamine receptor signaling
KRAS mutation is present in multiple sensitive lines and may interact with GPCR/dopamine pathways
CDKN2A loss is common in sensitive lines and may reduce cell cycle checkpoint control, enhancing drug effect
NF2 mutation appears in several least-affected lines, suggesting it may reduce sensitivity
KMT2D mutation is enriched in least-affected lines, possibly reflecting a chromatin state that buffers dopamine signaling
CTNNB1 mutation appears in least-affected lines and may indicate Wnt-driven resistance
